decisions.reason: Canonical 2012-01 constituency geometry already produces a complete reproducible boundary-derived area series. County official area is not inherited downward.
Canonical 2012-01 ward geometry already produces a complete reproducible boundary-derived area series. Parent area is not inherited downward.
Canonical constituency values are exact sums of official IEBC Gazette Notice No. 7290 child-ward register rows under the established P23 contract.

IEBC Gazette Notice No. 7290 publishes the ward register directly. The Atlas already materialises 1,440 confidently mapped ward rows; the ten Mandera East/Lafey source rows remain explicitly withheld from canonical ward geometry until the spatial hold is reconciled rather than force-matched or inherited.

KNBS Gross County Product is an official county economic-accounting product. No compatible official current-290 constituency GCP allocation is published, and allocating county GCP by population, land area or equal shares would manufacture local economic output.
KNBS Gross County Product is published at county level. No official ward GCP allocation exists in the governed source, and parent GCP cannot be divided or inherited to wards.

Agriculture GVA is sourced from county economic accounts. The source does not publish current electoral-constituency GVA, and no governed small-area production model has been approved for deterministic disaggregation.
Agriculture GVA is a county-accounting measure in the governed source. Ward values cannot be inferred by land area, population or equal allocation without fabricating local output.
Manufacturing GVA is published through county economic accounts, not current electoral constituencies. No source-backed constituency allocation or approved small-area model is available.
Manufacturing GVA is a county economic-accounting measure. Ward values are not published and cannot be proportionally inherited from the county total.

Agriculture share of GCP requires a constituency agriculture numerator and constituency GCP denominator on the same accounting basis. Neither is published for the current 290 constituencies, so the county share cannot be inherited.
Agriculture share of GCP requires matched ward numerator and denominator economic accounts. Those are not published in the governed source, and the county percentage cannot be copied downward.

Manufacturing share of GCP requires matched constituency manufacturing GVA and total GCP. The official county accounts do not publish these for current constituencies, so no local percentage is defensible.
Manufacturing share of GCP requires matched ward manufacturing GVA and total GCP. Neither is published, and county shares must not be inherited to wards.

The canonical estimate is a KDHS county-domain survey estimate with published weighting and denominator semantics. The Atlas has no official current-constituency estimate or survey design supporting direct constituency publication; county survey rates cannot be inherited or naively reweighted.
The KDHS county-domain estimate is not designed as a ward estimate. No official ward-domain estimate is published, and downscaling a county survey rate would misstate sampling precision.

The canonical home-birth rate is a KDHS county-domain survey estimate. No official constituency-domain rate with compatible weighting and denominator is published, so the county rate cannot be inherited.
The KDHS estimate is not a ward-domain statistic. Publishing the county percentage at ward level, or recomputing it without the survey design and valid domain sample, would be misleading.

Modern contraceptive use is published canonically as a KDHS county-domain estimate. No official current-constituency domain estimate is available in the governed source, and parent survey estimates cannot be inherited.
Modern contraceptive use is a survey estimate whose published domain is county. No valid official ward estimate is available; county values cannot be copied or proportionally allocated to wards.

The canonical FGM measure is a sensitive KDHS county-domain estimate with ranking withheld. No official current-constituency estimate with valid survey precision is published, so local downscaling is prohibited.

The canonical FGM measure is not a ward-domain estimate. Inheriting or modelling the county percentage at ward level without an approved survey-domain method would create false precision for a sensitive indicator.

The canonical HIV prevalence series uses KENPHIA county estimates with published uncertainty. No official current-constituency prevalence estimates with comparable uncertainty are available in the governed source, so county prevalence cannot be inherited.
KENPHIA prevalence is not published as a ward-domain estimate. Downscaling a county prevalence rate would create unsupported local precision and is prohibited under the cascade contract.

The canonical child-stunting rate is a KDHS county-domain survey estimate. KDHS 2022 does not publish a current-290 constituency-domain estimate with survey precision adequate for Atlas publication, so the county rate cannot be inherited or naively reweighted.

The KDHS child-stunting estimate is not a ward-domain statistic. Copying or downscaling the county survey percentage would create unsupported local precision and is prohibited by the cascade contract.

Skilled birth attendance is canonically defined from KDHS 2022 survey estimates. No official current-constituency domain estimate with compatible survey weighting is published, so county values cannot be inherited to constituencies.
KDHS 2022 skilled birth attendance is not published as a ward-domain estimate. Ward publication would require a valid domain sample and weighting design rather than copying the county percentage.

Basic immunisation is canonically defined from KDHS 2022 Table 10.4C for children age 12–23 months. No official current-constituency domain estimate with compatible survey weighting is published, so the county estimate cannot be inherited.
The KDHS 2022 basic-immunisation estimate is not a ward-domain statistic. Downscaling the county rate without the survey design and valid ward-domain sample would create false precision.
